cohort: 357 deceased mothers in West Bengal, India, with 317 identified via facility-based data and 40 from community-based maternal death review; in-depth interviews were also conducted among 12 caregivers of the deceased mothers.
finding: Eclampsia accounts for one-third of maternal deaths in West Bengal, and several factors, including younger age, primigravida or nulliparous status, lack of antenatal care, and rural residence, increase the risk.
mod_finding: The risk of death due to eclampsia was two times higher among women who had a cesarean section compared to those who did not.
